title: Solve equations that need the distributive property first (3(x − 4) = 2x + 1)

lesson.title: Clear the Brackets First: 3(x − 4) = 2x + 1

steps.say: You already know how to solve something like two times, bracket, x plus four, close bracket, equals negative six. Today the twist is that x shows up on both sides of the scale. The equation is three times, bracket, x minus four, close bracket, equals two x plus one. The plan is simple: clear the brackets first, then balance like usual.

visual.caption: Both sides weigh the same, but the left side is wrapped in brackets

steps.say: Step one: distribute. The three multiplies every term inside the brackets, not just the first one. Three times x is three x. Three times negative four is negative twelve. So the left side becomes three x minus twelve. Nothing changed in weight, we just unpacked it.

visual.caption: Same weight on the left, just unpacked: 3x − 12

steps.say: Step two: get the x terms together on one side. Both sides have some x's, so take two x off both pans. Three x minus two x leaves one x on the left. Two x minus two x leaves zero on the right, so the right is just one. Now the scale reads x minus twelve equals one.

visual.caption: After taking 2x off both sides, the scale still balances

steps.say: Step three: undo the minus twelve by adding twelve to both sides. Left side: x minus twelve plus twelve is just x. Right side: one plus twelve is thirteen. So x equals thirteen. Quick check: three times, bracket, thirteen minus four, is three times nine, which is twenty-seven. And two times thirteen plus one is twenty-six plus one, also twenty-seven. Both sides match, so thirteen is right.

visual.caption: Add 12 to both pans and x stands alone: x = 13

steps.say: Here is the mistake that costs people the most marks: distributing to only the first term. Someone writes three times, bracket, x minus four, as three x minus four. But they forgot to multiply the four by three. Think of it like a group chat with three friends each chipping in x dollars and each paying a four dollar fee. The total fee is twelve dollars, not four. The bracket means the three multiplies everything inside.

visual.caption: Three rows of (x and 4): the 3 multiplies both parts, giving 3x + 3(4)

steps.say: One more trap: doing something to one side only. If you have three x equals twelve and just write x equals twelve, you took the three off the left but did nothing to the right, so the scale tips. Whatever you do, do it to both pans. Takeaway: distribute to every term, then keep the scale balanced by doing every move on both sides.

visual.caption: Dividing only the left side by 3 tips the scale: x = 12 is wrong, x = 4 is right

lesson.answer: Distribute to EVERY term in the brackets, then do each move to BOTH sides.

practice.question: Picture a balance scale. The left pan holds four times, bracket, x minus two, close bracket. The right pan holds two x plus six. It is perfectly balanced. Solve for x, and then check your answer in both pans. Hint: the x could stand for dollars in a shared bus fare.
practice.answer: Distribute: 4x − 8 = 2x + 6. Take 2x off both sides: 2x − 8 = 6. Add 8 to both sides: 2x = 14. Divide both sides by 2: x = 7. Check: 4(7 − 2) = 4 × 5 = 20 and 2(7) + 6 = 20. Balanced!
